finding.title: Login code textbox has no accessible name

oracle.evidence: [qa-layout] unnamed-control textbox "after If you received a code to log in, enter "

steps: Enter a fresh email and press Enter
Code entry screen appears
finding.expected: The code text field has an accessible name
finding.actual: The code textbox (below 'If you received a code to log in, enter it here:') has no name in the snapshot; probe reports unnamed-control

judge.reason: The layout probe reports an unnamed-control textbox located after 'If you received a code to log in, enter' on the login code screen. The replay reproduced the same line, and the finding's actual describes that code field. A screen reader user cannot identify the field needed to sign in.

finding.title: Onboarding back (arrow-left) button has no accessible name

oracle.evidence: [qa-layout] unnamed-control button "arrow-left icon after Connect Google"

steps: Sign in with fresh address on onboarding build
Agree to the terms and press Continue
On the Connect Google step, look at the arrow-left button at bottom left of the dialog
finding.expected: The back button has an accessible name such as Back
finding.actual: The arrow-left icon button next to Skip/Continue has no name; the probe reports unnamed-control

judge.reason: The layout probe reports an unnamed-control for the arrow-left icon button after the 'Connect Google' heading, and the replay failure shows the same line. The finding's actual describes that same back button, so a screen reader user cannot identify the onboarding back control.

finding.title: Onboarding location dropdown has no accessible name

oracle.evidence: [qa-layout] unnamed-control combobox "chevron-down icon after This helps us personalize your experienc"

steps: Sign in with a fresh address
Accept privacy, Continue, Skip Connect Google, Continue the name step
Look at the 'Where are you located?' step
finding.expected: The location combobox has an accessible name
finding.actual: The 'Select location…' combobox is reported by the probe as an unnamed control

judge.reason: The layout probe reports an unnamed combobox (chevron-down icon after the 'This helps us personalize your experience' text) on the 'Where are you located?' onboarding step. The replay reproduced the same line after reaching that heading, and the finding's 'Select location…' combobox matches that control. Screen reader users cannot identify the field in the onboarding flow.

finding.title: Onboarding back arrow button has no accessible name

Tick the privacy checkbox and press Continue
On the Connect Google step see the back arrow button at bottom left
finding.expected: Back button has an accessible name (e.g. Back)
finding.actual: The bottom-left arrow-left button on the Connect Google step ([49,2254][160,2373]) has no text or a11y label

The finding's actual describes that control, the arrow-left back button after the Connect Google text, which has no accessible name for screen reader users.

finding.title: Name field on onboarding is hidden behind the keyboard
steps: Sign in with a fresh address
Accept privacy, Continue, Skip Connect Google
On What should we call you? the name field autofocuses and the keyboard opens
finding.expected: Focused name field stays fully visible above the keyboard
finding.actual: The Enter your name field is cut by the keyboard (only its top half visible), Continue button not reachable without hiding keyboard

judge.reason: The replay hit the same layout probe line, [qa-layout] behind-keyboard textbox "Enter your name", and the repro reaches the "What should we call you?" onboarding screen on Android. The focused name field is covered by the keyboard during first-run onboarding.
